title: The twists $\mathcal O(d)$ exist
statement:
Let $k$ be a field, $d\in\mathbf Z$, and let
$U_0,U_1,U_{01}$ be the standard affine cover of
$\mathbf P^1_k$ of [def-sc-p1-standard]. Then a twisted
structure sheaf $\mathcal O(d)$ as in
[def-sc-p1-standard] exists, and it is an
invertible
$\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^1_k}$-module; it is unique up to unique
isomorphism compatible with the generating sections $g_0,g_1$.

proof.text: On $U_0$ and $U_1$ take the free rank-one modules generated by $g_0$ and $g_1$. On $U_{01}$ define the transition map by $g_0\mapsto t^{-d}g_1$. By [def-sc-p1-standard], $\Gamma(U_{01},\mathcal O)=k[t,t^{-1}]$, and $t^{-d}$ is a unit with inverse $t^d$, so this is an $\mathcal O_{U_{01}}$-linear isomorphism.

For the self-overlaps set the transition maps to the identity, so $\varphi_{00}=\varphi_{11}=\operatorname{id}$. On the two-member cover, every nontrivial triple overlap is $U_{01}$, and the remaining cocycle identities reduce to $t^d\,t^{-d}=1$ and $t^{-d}\,t^d=1$ there; they hold because the two transition units are inverse. Thus all transition maps satisfy the cocycle condition required for sheaf gluing.

Apply clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-glue-sheaves-of-modules] to the cover $\{U_0,U_1\}$ and these two free modules and transition isomorphisms. It gives an $\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^1_k}$-module $\mathcal O(d)$ and isomorphisms from its restrictions to the two local modules, compatible with the transition map. Each local module is the free module $\mathcal O_{U_i}$, hence is quasi-coherent; quasi-coherence is local on this cover, so the glued module is quasi-coherent. The same local isomorphisms make it locally free of rank one, hence invertible by [def-sc-invertible-module].

If $\mathcal O'(d)$ is another glued module with local generators satisfying the same transition relation, the two chosen local identifications define maps between the restrictions of $\mathcal O(d)$ and $\mathcal O'(d)$ that agree on $U_{01}$. Clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-glue-sheaves-of-modules] glues them to a unique global isomorphism compatible with $g_0,g_1$; gluing the inverse local maps gives its inverse. Hence the glued twist is unique up to unique compatible isomorphism.
